title: Listen to the Latest ‘KFF Health News Minute’
summary: The "KFF Health News Minute" brings original healthcare and health policy reporting from our newsroom to the airwaves each week.

title: Readers Speak Out on Work Requirements, Federal Data Grab, Opioid Payback Cash
summary: KFF Health News gives readers a chance to comment on a recent batch of stories.

title: People With Disabilities Say Medicaid’s Limits on Income Stifle Career Advancement
summary: Special Medicaid programs in many states allow disabled people to work while receiving benefits, and most limit how much participants can earn and the assets they can hold. Some Iowans are pushing lawmakers to remove those limits, which they say can dampen their career prospects.

title: Years After He Quit Smoking, a Lung Cancer Scan Saved His Life
summary: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer deaths in the United States, and older adults are at higher risk. But only about a quarter of patients eligible for screening are up to date.

title: Hospitals Say They Found a Tool To Help Reduce Childbirth Risks: Wristbands
summary: North Carolina and other states have embraced “I Gave Birth” wristbands as a way to encourage women to seek help when they have postpartum complications. They’re gaining steam as the Trump administration’s cuts to Medicaid threaten postpartum care.

title: Hospital Prepayment Requirements Add New Wrinkles to Patients’ Financial Responsibility
summary: Hospitals and other medical providers are increasingly asking for payment before providing care, collecting more of what patients might owe as rising insurance deductibles add to Americans' financial pressures.

title: A Federal Policy Is Complicating How Organizations Battle the Opioid Crisis
summary: Drug test strips are credited with saving lives, but a new policy will limit how funds can be used for them. Advocates of harm reduction strategies who responded to a mass overdose in Baltimore say distributing them will get harder. Federal officials say the strips enable drug use.

title: Patients Wary of Governments, Companies Pushing AI as a Rural Healthcare Solution
summary: The $50 billion federal Rural Health Transformation Program is set to flood rural America with new AI health tools. That’s despite little evidence on whether health-related AI can improve access to care and patient health in those communities.

title: Many States Cover Doula Care, but Access to a ‘Birthing Bestie’ Is Often Out of Reach
summary: Virginia Medicaid started covering doula care four years ago. But logistical and administrative challenges leave many expectant parents without the support of a doula.

title: Same Knee Surgery, Twice the Price: Hospital Monopolies Push Up Healthcare Costs
summary: A federal disclosure rule is offering new insight on the effect of healthcare monopolies on pricing, following a wave of U.S. mergers.
